jobs.title: Director, Scale-up & Engineering
jobs.description:
Here’s What All The Hype Is About…

Premier Nutrition Company (PNC) is one of the fastest-growing companies in the proactive wellness space showing clear leadership in the category of protein shakes and powders. We make the brands Premier Protein and Dymatize , and are part of our publicly traded holding company, BellRing Brands (NYSE: BRBR).

We have a simple, yet powerful, formula for our success, which we’ve been nailing since our founding in 1997. We start with an organization powered by our company purpose— Changing Lives with Good Energy . Then our purpose-driven people are given the support and autonomy to develop and grow. Next, we are super-intentional about designing a culture where everyone feels like they truly connect and belong , which is one of our five company core values. Purpose-driven, connected employees deliver amazing business results. And winning companies with remarkable people and thriving cultures attract and retain top talent, so the cycle becomes self-reinforcing or what we call our regenerative culture .

We don’t mind sharing our formula, since we believe the world would be a better place if more workplaces treated adults like adults and gave them the platform to do the best work of their lives—alongside some truly amazing colleagues. Why don’t more companies do this? It takes deep-in-your-bones conviction to your people, products, and purpose to pull it off. It also takes resisting the urge to try to control people, and instead, trusting them to make the right decisions. The result of our vibrant culture speaks for itself: We were certified as a Great Place to Work ™ for the 9 th year-running in 2025. And we currently rank #8 on Fortune Magazine’s Best Workplaces in our category and were in the top 12 for each of the last 7 years.

We have a long list of ways we take care of our people, but here are some crowd-pleasers that our employees often say they love most: Year-round ½ day Fridays, in-office massages, free lunches & snacks, dogs in the office, culture of belonging celebrations, engaging in-office events like bring your kids to work day, 6% 401k match after 1 year, generous paid family leave regardless of gender, all positions bonus-eligible, company-wide volunteer days, company-matched charitable donations, no employee handbook, no dress code, coaching conversations instead of performance reviews, and walking meetings.

PNC seeks individuals who will flourish in this type of work environment and will add to our culture and help build this high-growth company for the next phase in our amazing journey. Does this sound like you? Then read on…

We believe in the power of mindset, and specifically what we call the Challenger Mindset . Do you take smart, bold risks, display relentless hunger, and see yourself as a builder? We’re looking for individuals who choose action over analysis paralysis—those who start before they feel completely ready, make calculated moves based on the best information available, and build momentum through decisive action rather than perfect planning. You should have an insatiable drive that keeps you agile and forward-thinking, always challenging assumptions, seeking new opportunities, and focusing on long-term impact over short-term wins. Above all, you’re a builder—someone who transforms the status quo, finds smarter, simpler, faster ways to get things done, and inspires others to do the same.

The role you’re interested in…

The successful candidate will be an experienced R&D leader who provides strategic direction and technical oversight for scale-up, process engineering, packaging engineering and manufacturing support activities. This role will lead pilot plant operations (internal and external), scale-up efforts at co-manufacturing facilities, and process and packaging improvement initiatives focused on cost optimization and operational efficiency.

The position will lead a team of 5-10 technical professionals and technicians, ensuring pilot plant, scale-up and packaging activities align with business objectives and enable a seamless transition from product/package development, through commercialization. Responsibilities include establishing robust scale-up processes, supporting manufacturing troubleshooting, and ensuring products can be efficiently and reliably produced at commercial scale.

Success in this role requires strong cross-functional leadership and shared accountability for project outcomes. The leader will build effective partnerships with internal stakeholders, co-manufacturers, and external service providers to drive projects from development through successful commercialization. This role reports into our VP, Product Development.

If you are ready to flex your thinking between technical problem solving, guiding, enhance scale up program, and coaching team members, then welcome aboard.

The work environment…

So, what’s it like to work here? If you’re based in the greater Bay Area, you’ll walk into our Emeryville office each Tuesday morning and start the in-person portion of our hybrid work week at our weekly all-company meeting and find close to 200 of your colleagues, some sitting with their dogs, talking excitedly through the week ahead and watching a newer teammate tell their personal life and career journey followed by a quick update on any hot topics that might be relevant to the week ahead.

We are a dynamic, HYBRID workplace, with an expectation that all employees come into the office Tuesday through Thursday. We are very intentional about connecting in person for things like innovation, impromptu collaboration, having respectful challenges to get to better decisions, leadership role-modeling, and culture building. Great work cultures are built on stories about what great looks like in practice, and great stories during virtual meetings just don’t happen. The expected pay scale for this role is $200k to $220k, which may vary based on relevant experience, qualifications, geographic area (if applicable), and internal equity for the role.

At the beginning of 2026, we moved into our massive modern 133,000 square foot headquarters in Emeryville, California, complete with spacious personal workspaces, gym with rock-climbing wall, a café, free onsite parking, tons of greenery, and many transportation options.

You’re excited about this opportunity because your time will be filled with…

Critical Thinking & Technical Leadership: 40% of your time

Lead scale-up, commercialization, pilot plant operations, and manufacturing support activities
Drive continuous improvement of scale-up and commercialization processes to ensure efficient transitions from development to production
Build strategic partnerships with co-manufacturers and external service providers to ensure R&D objectives are met
Oversee and integrate technical packaging activities in scale-up and commercialization initiatives
Provide technical leadership in processing, manufacturing performance, packaging engineering, risk management, and problem-solving
Ensure product, package and process compliance through collaboration with cross-functional partners
Identify emerging technologies, trends, and external capabilities to strengthen R&D and commercialization
Provide input on long-term capability, equipment, facility, and talent needs

R&I People Leadership & Culture: 40% of your time

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing technical team
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous learning
Manage resource allocation and priorities to ensure successful project execution
Contribute as an active member of the R&I Leadership Team
Build strong partnerships across functions and external organizations to drive project success
Represent and advocates for R&I by providing technical insight, strategic thinking, and leadership across the business

The daily stuff that everyone does but few quantify: 20% of your time

Attending meetings and presentations
Participating in company-wide activities and events galore
Impromptu conversations with colleagues
Administrivia like email, calendaring, expense reports, and other non-value-added work

What are we looking for?

Ability to explain complex technical subject matters to non-technical team
Ability to apply technical know-out to real world problems
Ability to drive results, pivot quickly as needed
Strong collaborative skills and ability to work well in teams
Possess curiosity, creativity, and alternative thinking to develop better or new solutions with a scientific approach

Education

Bachelor’s degree Food Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Biological Sciences, Food Science or similar field

Experience

12+ years of experience in the food and beverage industry, including thermal processing and aseptic beverage processing, and high-protein RTD scale-up.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing technical teams.
Demonstrated success commercializing products (product, process, package) through co-manufacturing partners and supporting manufacturing operations.
Strong technical troubleshooting and process optimization capabilities.
Working knowledge (incl. Mechanical) of processing and packaging equipment and manufacturing systems (batching through packaging)
Strong working knowledge of process capability studies, statistical process control and specifications – ability to read, design and interpret specifications

Skills And Mindset

Strong ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders across all levels of external manufacturing organizations
Ability to translate complex technical information into clear business recommendations and drive decision-making
Proven cross-functional leadership and project management skills with a track record of delivering results through internal and external teams
Demonstrated experience managing project risk, solving complex technical challenges, and executing against timelines
Excellent communication, collaboration, and influencing skills
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing multiple priorities
Willingness to travel up to 35%

What The Work Is Like

You'll spend a significant portion of your day working on a computer, reviewing data, creating reports, communicating with partners, and joining virtual and in-person meetings
This role requires frequent and ongoing use of a keyboard, mouse, phone, and other office technology
You'll regularly navigate multiple systems at once, analyze detailed information, and shift between competing priorities and deadlines
You'll communicate regularly with team members, cross-functional partners, external partners, and leaders through meetings, Outlook based email, messaging platforms such as Microsoft Teams, and presentations
Occasional movement around the office may be required for meetings, collaboration, and team activities
May occasionally lift or move office materials weighing up to 10 pounds

So, if after reading through this long list you’re thinking—I’m not sure I meet 100% of these requirements, should I still apply? YES—if you embody a growth mindset, see challenges as opportunities to develop, and find innovative ways to get the real work that matters done, you sound like our kind of candidate!

The 5 capabilities or mindsets most relevant to this role:

Emotional intelligence
Thrive in ambiguity amid competing priorities
Connect & Belong
Play to Win
Creativity, exploration, & innovativeness

You will thrive here and may just do the best work of your life if…

You want to be an integral part of shaping and nurturing an amazing work culture
You can be flexible in your approach to challenges and abandon past practices if they don’t make sense or lead to a poor outcome
You are comfortable being natural, casual, open, and even a bit playful at work
You don’t have a big ego and hate siloed thinking
You can be friendly, vulnerable, and self-deprecating in one moment, and deal with a challenging, delicate people-related matter as a professional in the next

jobs.title: Director, Test Engineering
jobs.description:
Own Every Moment at NetApp

At NetApp, your ideas power innovation. We lead in intelligent data infrastructure—delivering unified storage, integrated data services, and solutions that help organizations unlock the full potential of their data, from AI to multicloud.

Ready to innovate and contribute to our path to $10B? Here, you'll collaborate with passionate teams, tackle real-world challenges, and see your impact in how customers transform and grow. If you're ready to bring curiosity, creativity, and drive to every moment, NetApp is where your journey begins. Join teams that innovate to elevate, drive results, and excel together across every function.

Position Summary

The Director, Test Engineering is responsible for leading NetApp's PCBA Manufacturing Test Engineering organization, ensuring products are designed, validated, and manufactured to meet the highest standards of quality, reliability, manufacturability, and operational efficiency. This position leads the engineering team responsible for In-Circuit Test (ICT), Boundary Scan Test (BST), Functional Verification Test (FVT), and Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) across both New Product Introduction (NPI) programs and sustaining manufacturing operations.

Reporting directly to the VP, Ops Engineering, the Director will drive manufacturing test strategy, execution, automation, quality improvements, factory yield optimization, and continuous process improvement initiatives in partnership with engineering, operations, supply chain, and manufacturing partners worldwide.

The Director leads an organization consisting of one engineering manager and a total team of approximately eleven engineers located in San Jose, CA, Wichita, KS, and Taipei, Taiwan, while driving a portfolio of strategic initiatives focused on improving product quality, manufacturing efficiency, test coverage, cost, and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities

Define and execute the company's PCBA manufacturing test strategy across ICT, BST, FVT, and ESS.
Lead manufacturing test development and deployment for all NPI programs, ensuring test readiness, quality objectives, schedule commitments, and successful production ramps.
Drive continuous improvement of sustaining manufacturing test processes, methodologies, automation, coverage, efficiency, and factory yields.
Lead and develop a high-performing engineering organization consisting of managers and individual contributors across multiple geographies.
Partner closely with Hardware Engineering, Firmware Engineering, Software Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, Supplier Quality Engineering, and Operations teams to ensure robust test coverage throughout the product lifecycle.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators related to test coverage, yield performance, test efficiency, quality escape prevention, first-pass yield, cycle time, and manufacturing readiness.
Drive root cause investigations and corrective actions for manufacturing test failures, yield excursions, and field quality issues.
Oversee test architecture, hardware, software, automation frameworks, fixtures, instrumentation, diagnostics, and manufacturing data analysis.
Lead engagement with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and external engineering partners to ensure global manufacturing test excellence.
Drive a portfolio of continuous improvement initiatives focused on operational efficiency, quality improvement, manufacturing scalability, cost reduction, and test optimization.
Champion Design for Testability (DFT), Design for Manufacturability (DFM), and Design for Quality (DFQ) practices across product development programs.
Establish organizational roadmaps, budgets, staffing plans, and resource strategies aligned with business priorities.
Prepare and present executive-level updates, metrics, risks, recommendations, and strategic plans to senior leadership.

Leadership Responsibilities

Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and performance management for managers and engineers.
Build a culture centered on accountability, technical excellence, innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Develop succession plans and organizational capability to support future business growth.
Foster strong cross-functional partnerships and influence decision-making across engineering and operations organizations.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
Minimum of 15 years of experience in engineering, manufacturing test engineering, product validation, or related technical functions.
Minimum of 8 years of people leadership experience, including management of managers and technical teams.
Strong expertise in PCBA manufacturing test methodologies, including ICT, BST, FVT, and ESS.
Experience supporting both New Product Introduction (NPI) programs and sustaining manufacturing operations.
Demonstrated success driving manufacturing quality, yield improvement, defect reduction, and operational excellence initiatives.
Experience working with global manufacturing partners, suppliers, contract manufacturers, and cross-functional engineering organizations.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, and organizational skills.
Excellent verbal, written, and executive communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Experience with enterprise storage systems, networking products, server platforms, or other complex electronic systems.
Experience implementing manufacturing test automation, data analytics, and advanced diagnostic methodologies.
Proven track record of leading large-scale engineering transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
Lean, Six Sigma, or related continuous improvement certification.

What Success Looks Like

Successful delivery of manufacturing test solutions for all NPI programs.
Sustained improvements in factory yield, quality, test coverage, efficiency, and cost.
Execution of strategic test engineering improvement initiatives.
Strong organizational capability, employee development, and leadership bench strength.
Effective partnership across engineering, operations, and manufacturing organizations to support business growth and operational excellence.

Compensation:

The target salary range for this position is 196,350 - 292,600 USD. The salary offered will be determined by the candidate's location, qualifications, experience, and education and may be outside of this range. The range is based on 'On Target Earnings’ (OTE) representing the total potential earnings, which is the sum of the base salary and potential commission earned when performance targets are achieved. Final compensation packages are competitive and in line with industry standards, reflecting a variety of factors, and include a comprehensive benefits package. This may cover Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Retirement or Pension Plans, Paid Time Off, various Leave options, employee stock purchase plan, and/or restricted stocks (RSU’s). These offerings are subject to regional variations and governed by local laws, regulations, and company policies. We will provide detailed information about the specific benefits for your region during the recruitment process.

At NetApp, we embrace a hybrid working environment designed to strengthen connection, collaboration, and culture for all employees. This means that most roles will have some level of in-office and/or in-person expectations, which will be shared during the recruitment process.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

NetApp is firmly committed to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and to compliance with all federal, state and local laws that prohibit employment discrimination based on age, race, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, religion, disability or genetic information, pregnancy, protected veteran status, and any other protected classification.

Why You'll Thrive at NetApp

At NetApp, you won't wait for the perfect moment—you'll make it. The early planning, the extra thought, the bold idea that turns good into great: That's how our people operate and how we continue to push the boundaries of data infrastructure.

NetApp is the trusted partner for organizations transforming data into opportunity. As the only enterprise-grade storage service natively embedded in Google Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure, we empower customers to run everything from traditional workloads to enterprise AI with unmatched performance, resilience, and security.

Our culture

We celebrate mold breakers, bold thinkers, and problem solvers. We reward initiative, impact, and ownership. We provide flexibility so you can balance professional ambition with your personal life. Here, differences are not just welcomed—they drive everything we do.

If you're ready to innovate, rise to the challenge, and own every moment - make your next move your best one. Apply now.

Submitting an Application

To ensure a streamlined and fair hiring process for all candidates, our team only reviews applications submitted through our company website. This practice allows us to track, assess, and respond to applicants efficiently. Emailing our employees, recruiters, or Human Resources personnel directly will not influence your application.

About The Department:

George Mason University has experienced rapid growth over the past several years, resulting in R1 classification, a significant increase in invention disclosures, and a growing portfolio of maturing technologies. With the continued expansion of the regional innovation ecosystem and numerous technology-driven companies in Northern Virginia, the University is advancing its technology transfer and commercialization infrastructure.

The Office of Technology Transfer sits in Mason Enterprise, part of the Office of Research, Innovation, and Economic Impact, which leads university-wide efforts related to innovation, commercialization, entrepreneurship, and industry engagement. The University continues to build a more holistic innovation and business development function to better serve faculty and student innovators, deepen industry partnerships, and contribute to the region’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.

About The Position:

The Senior Director, Technology Transfer supports the Office of Research, Innovation, and Economic Impact's growth. This position reflects a refined, execution-focused leadership model while maintaining strategic responsibility for technology transfer across the University. The Senior Director will play a critical role in translating George Mason’s research discoveries into societal and economic impact through intellectual property protection, commercialization, industry engagement, and startup support. This position fits within George Mason’s highly collaborative and inclusive culture and strongly supports the University’s commitment to research commercialization and entrepreneurship.

The Senior Director, Technology Transfer leads the University’s efforts to facilitate the transfer of research discoveries and innovations for public use and benefit. The Senior Director establishes and implements strategies, tools, and procedures to evaluate, protect, market, and commercialize technologies developed by faculty and students. The position has responsibility for technology transfer across all George Mason University campuses.

This role requires independent decision-making authority that substantially affects business operations. The Senior Director reports to the Associate Vice President for Innovation and Economic Development and works closely with faculty, university leadership, legal counsel, industry partners, investors, and external stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

Technology Transfer & Intellectual Property Management:

Lead and oversee the assessment, protection, and management of intellectual property, including inventions, software, data, and other research outputs;
Guide patenting and IP strategy in collaboration with internal stakeholders and external legal counsel;
Oversee the evaluation of invention disclosures for commercial potential and prioritize technologies for investment and advancement;
Lead negotiation and execution of license agreements, option agreements, NDAs, MTAs, and other IP-related contracts; and
Assist the Office of Sponsored Programs and University Counsel with intellectual property clauses in university agreements.

Technology Transfer Operations, Strategy & Team Leadership:

Coordinate with the Associate Vice President to lead operational functions and new initiatives aligned with university strategy;
Recommend and implement streamlined procedures, systems, and best practices for technology transfer operations;
Manage staff and build a high-performing team to support invention intake, IP management, licensing, and industry engagement;
Maintain and enhance reporting, project management, and database systems related to commercialization activities;
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and outside counsel; and
Assist the Vice President of Research with George Mason Research Foundation operations.

Compliance, Policy & Stakeholder Communication:

Ensure compliance with federal regulations, including Bayh–Dole requirements, conflict-of-interest policies, and reporting obligations;
Communicate technology transfer policies and processes to faculty in a manner that fosters understanding, trust, and collaboration; and
Prepare and present reports to university leadership as required.

Industry Partnerships & Commercialization Strategy:

Serve as a liaison between faculty and industry partners to identify and align industry-relevant research opportunities;
Cultivate and manage relationships with corporations, startups, investors, venture capital firms, accelerators, and government agencies; and
Promote George Mason technologies through targeted outreach, meetings, presentations, and strategic partnerships.

Entrepreneurship & Innovation Ecosystem Development:

Support faculty and student entrepreneurs in navigating commercialization pathways;
Collaborate with campus entrepreneurship programs, incubators, and economic development organizations; and
Provide strategic guidance to university-affiliated startups and help reduce barriers to startup formation and growth.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in science or engineering, and business or law, or related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience;
Significant experience (generally at least 10 years) in technology transfer, intellectual property management, licensing, business development, or a related field within a research-intensive environment;
Generally, at least 5 years of proven leadership and people management skills;
Knowledge of technology transfer, intellectual property management, licensing, business development, or a related field within a research-intensive environment;
Demonstrated skill and success negotiating complex contracts and managing patent expenses;
Strong understanding/knowledge of the university research environment and ability to translate between academic research and industry needs;
Demonstrated team leadership and people management skills;
Ability to translate complex technical research into clear, non-confidential technology descriptions;
Demonstrated strategic thinking, sound judgment, and ability to work independently in a collaborative environment;
Excellent written and verbal communication skills;
Strong organizational abilities;
Proficiency with MS Office and CRM or database systems; and
Ability to exercise discretion and maintain confidentiality.

Preferred Qualifications:

The Senior Director, Technology Transfer supports the Office of Research, Innovation, and Economic Impact's growth. The Senior Director will play a critical role in translating George Mason’s research discoveries into societal and economic impact through intellectual property protection, commercialization, industry engagement, and startup support. The Senior Director, Technology Transfer leads the University’s efforts to facilitate the transfer of research discoveries and innovations for public use and benefit. Recommend and implement streamlined procedures, systems, and best practices for technology transfer operations;

Maintain and enhance reporting, project management, and database systems related to commercialization activities;
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and outside counsel; and
Assist the Vice President of Research with George Mason Research Foundation operations.

Communicate technology transfer policies and processes to faculty in a manner that fosters understanding, trust, and collaboration; and
Prepare and present reports to university leadership as required.

Serve as a liaison between faculty and industry partners to identify and align industry-relevant research opportunities;
Cultivate and manage relationships with corporations, startups, investors, venture capital firms, accelerators, and government agencies; and
Promote George Mason technologies through targeted outreach, meetings, presentations, and strategic partnerships.

Entrepreneurship & Innovation Ecosystem Development:

Support faculty and student entrepreneurs in navigating commercialization pathways;
Collaborate with campus entrepreneurship programs, incubators, and economic development organizations; and
Provide strategic guidance to university-affiliated startups and help reduce barriers to startup formation and growth.

Demonstrated strategic thinking, sound judgment, and ability to work independently in a collaborative environment;
Excellent written and verbal communication skills;
Strong organizational abilities;
Proficiency with MS Office and CRM or database systems; and

Background in computing, cybersecurity, bio-technology, engineering or other high-growth technology domains;

Experience developing or integrating applications within a Guidewire ecosystem (e.g., PolicyCenter, ClaimsCenter, Contact Manager)

Demonstrated ability to manage a broad portfolio of production applications in a complex enterprise environment

Experience with complex and fast paced large scale transformations that spans across Business and Technology, in P&C Insurance.
Experience with large-scale mainframe system migrations to modern cloud-based SaaS platforms.
Experience working with matrix organizations, leading teams across multiple locations utilizing the SAFe framework.

Job Description:

At Remitly, we believe everyone deserves the freedom to access, move, and manage their money wherever life takes them. Since 2011, we've tirelessly delivered on our promise to customers sending money globally, providing secure, simple, and reliable ways to manage their money, ensuring true peace of mind. Whether it's supporting loved ones back home, growing a business across continents, or pursuing new opportunities abroad, we're not just here to move money— we're here to move our global customers forward.

We're looking for builders, reimaginers, and global thinkers who want to work at the intersection of technology, trust, and transformation. If that's you and you're ready to do the most meaningful work of your career—we invite you to join over 2,800 passionate Remitlians worldwide who are united by our vision to transform lives with trusted financial services that transcend borders.

About the Role:

The way software gets built is changing faster than at any point in the last twenty years. At Remitly, we move money for millions of customers around the world, and how fast and well we do that depends on the platforms and tooling our builders use every day.

We're hiring a Director of Engineering to lead our App Platform team. You'll evolve the systems behind Remitly's web and native client experiences, including deep ownership of the platforms our iOS and Android teams build on — along with the tooling our engineers use to build our products and customer experiences.

Your mandate is to transform how we build, increasing the velocity of every engineering and product team at Remitly quarter over quarter.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set direction and grow leaders, while using the tools yourself, shipping and forming your own opinions from first contact. The teams winning right now aren't the ones with the best roadmaps. They're the ones shipping the third version while everyone else is debating the first.

You Will:

Transform how Remitly builds, increasing the velocity of every engineering and product team at the company
Improve the inner- and outer-loop surfaces closest to daily product development, including build systems, local development, and client infrastructure
Own the native mobile platform roadmap — architecture, build systems, release infrastructure, and developer tooling — for the teams building Remitly's iOS and Android experiences
Place thoughtful technical bets, run them as experiments, double down on what's working, and retire what isn't
Hire and develop senior managers, principal engineers, and builders who are equal parts platform operators and experimenters
Hold the operational, reliability, and quality bar for the platforms you own
Build a team culture that treats the rate of change in this industry as its single biggest asset

You Have:

8+ years of technical leadership experience, including 5+ leading multiple teams
History building and operating platforms and tooling that engineers actually use and prefer
Experience hiring and developing senior engineering managers and principal engineers
Track record leading native mobile platform organizations — iOS and Android — including release, build, and platform experience investments at scale
Concrete examples of moving your team or yourself ahead of a major industry shift rather than catching up after the fact
Comfort holding a thoughtful technical opinion in a room of executives, and translating business strategy into technical bets and back
Fluency with the current generation of AI-native developer tooling, and ideas about what comes next that go beyond "use the tools more"
Range: you can move from a flaky test in CI to a platform thesis without dropping either

Compensation Details.
The starting base salary range for this position is typically $240,000 - $300,000. In the U.S., Remitly employees are shareholders in our Company and equity is part of our total compensation plan.
Your recruiter can share more information about medical benefits offered, as well as other financial benefits and total compensation components offered with this role.

Our Benefits:

Flexible paid time off
Health, dental, and vision + 401k plan with company matching
Paid parental, medical, military and family care leave
Mental Health & Family Forming Benefits
Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
Continuing education and travel benefits

Our Connected Work Culture: Driving Innovation, Together

At Remitly, we believe that true innovation sparks when we come together. Our Connected Work Culture fosters dynamic in-person collaboration, where ideas ignite and challenging problems find solutions faster. For corporate team members, we have an in-office expectation of at least 50% of the time monthly, typically achieved by coming in three days a week. This creates a consistent, meaningful overlap that supports team norms and business needs. Managers also have the flexibility to set higher expectations based on their team's specific needs. These intentional in-office moments are vital for deepening relationships, fueling creativity, and ensuring your impact is felt where it matters most.
